# Enclii LLM Context Pointer

Generated: 2026-05-29

## Purpose

This pointer file gives LLM agents a stable, tool-agnostic map for working in this
repository without depending on vendor-specific instruction files.

## Canonical instruction order

1. `AGENTS.md`
2. `README.md` if present
3. `ECOSYSTEM.md` if present
4. Relevant files under `docs/`, `infra/`, `.github/workflows/`, and source
   directories for the specific task

## Agent compatibility

`AGENTS.md` is the source of truth. `CLAUDE.md` exists only to redirect Claude
and other legacy agent integrations to `AGENTS.md`.

## Enclii-first operations contract

Use Enclii web, API, or CLI for routine production provisioning, deployment,
observability, domain management, secrets, provider operations, scaling,
rollback, and remediation.

Raw `kubectl`, `helm`, SSH, provider CLIs/APIs, `docker exec`, and direct
container access are allowed only for platform bootstrap or documented
break-glass emergencies when Enclii is unavailable or lacks an implemented
adapter. Any break-glass use must record the actor, reason, target
service/environment, commands executed, result, and follow-up Enclii adapter
gap or incident link.

## Commercial GA program (May 2026)

Scoped Commercial GA target: ~100% by ~2026-07-14 (30-day SLO + legal publish).

Read in order for GA work:

1. `docs/production/COMMERCIAL_GA_MASTER_PLAN.md` — master blueprint
2. `docs/production/GA_READINESS_SCORECARD.md` — gate sign-off dashboard
3. `docs/production/REMAINING_OPS_GA.md` — ops task queue
4. `docs/production/COMMERCIAL_GA_TRACKER.md` — program tracker

Do not track independent GA task state outside these files (see `scripts/check-ga-doc-drift.py`).

Wave 0 Enclii-first ops: `scripts/wave0-ga-ops.sh`, `enclii admin ga-verify`, `make commercial-ga-proof`.

## Recent operating-contract changes (2026-08-27)

Three behaviors changed on this date; agents carrying older context will be
wrong about all three. (1) One-off job dispatch resolves Deployments by
`<name>` / `<name>-web` / `<namespace>-web` and turns deterministic admission
denials into a terminal `failed` status with `failure_reason` persisted — see
`docs/cli/commands/jobs.md`. (2) Tunnel-route writes are guarded: backends must
resolve to a live Service+port, changed rules are canaried and reverted on
dial failure, and manifest capture refuses domains declared under a Service-doc
name with no live workload (the 2026-08-27 identity-outage class). (3) The
reusable `build-publish.yml` (v1.0.0-alpha.5) derives digests from the
registry, not Actions artifacts, and its guard requires pins_written > 0.

## DNS, domains and CLI identity (2026-09-07)

Learned during a live tenant onboarding; an agent carrying older context will be
wrong about all of it.

- DNS records (`providers cloudflare dns-apply`): a record is keyed by
  **name + type only**. A second TXT or MX at the same name is applied as a
  destructive `update` of the first — the dry-run says `create`, the apply says
  `updated`, and the earlier record is gone (issue #530, hit live on
  2026-09-07: an SPF TXT destroyed a Proton ownership TXT). Multiple same-type
  records at one name must go through the Cloudflare dashboard as break-glass
  until that is fixed; a single record of a type at a name, including every
  CNAME, is safe. MX priority rides inside `--content` (`"10 mail.example.com"`);
  there is no `--priority`. `--type MX --apply` has answered 502 from the edge
  while its own dry-run planned cleanly — re-read the zone before retrying.
- Brand-host onboarding order (verified 2026-09-07): `domains add` **from the
  repo root** (the `-f` parser validates `spec.build.dockerfile` against
  `os.Getwd()`, not the manifest's directory) -> `dns-apply` proxied CNAME ->
  `tunnels-apply` (plan must show only a create for the new host) -> `dns-apply`
  the verification TXT -> `domains verify`. Then `zone-settings-apply` once the
  zone is active (`always_use_https`, `automatic_https_rewrites`,
  `min_tls_version=1.2`; verify `curl -sSI http://<host>/` -> 301). A
  manifest-only merge builds nothing, so no capture runs and a newly declared
  host does not become live. Full runbook:
  `docs/runbooks/DOMAIN_AND_EMAIL_DNS_ONBOARDING.md`.
- After a nameserver switch, clients on a stale resolver see NXDOMAIN for hosts
  that exist only in the new zone (and Cloudflare 1034 for a DNS-only host the
  old zone pointed at a CDN) for up to the old NS TTL. Do not cut over
  redirects, and do not "fix" a record that already reads correctly at the
  zone's own nameservers, until public resolvers agree.
- CLI: `enclii whoami`/`login`/`logout` print on **stderr** (cobra
  `cmd.Println` -> `OutOrStderr()`; the CLI never calls `SetOut`), so
  `whoami > file` captures nothing. `enclii login` resolves whichever Janua
  identity the browser session holds — log out of a client app first.
  `--tenant` and `providers porkbun ping` (#527) are **not** in
  `v1.0.0-alpha.8`; build from `main` until `v1.0.0-alpha.9`.
- Per-tenant Porkbun (#527): merging does NOT apply the Vault policy. Run
  `scripts/apply-switchyard-vault-policy-remote.sh` (token on stdin, never
  argv) before the first `--tenant` call, or it 403s and reads as "credentials
  missing". Recipe: `docs/infrastructure/porkbun-tenant-credentials.md`.


## Boundary

This is not a full repository ingest. It is a compact context pointer; task-specific work must still read the relevant source documents listed below.

## Maintenance

These files are maintained by `internal-devops/scripts/sync-agent-docs.py`.
If repo-specific long-form agent guidance is needed, put it in `AGENTS.md`,
not `CLAUDE.md`.
